name: Opus 5 carry
strategy: A 10-leg cross-asset carry book that earns spread and premium income rather than price appreciation - structured credit (JAAA/CLOZ), agency-MBS-vs-repo carry (NLY), EM currency and sovereign carry (EMLC/EMB), high-yield spread (SPHY), equity and VIX variance premium (SPYI/SVXY) and midstream distributions (AMLP) - funded by 13% cash at 4% APY, with the only short expressed as a 3%-margin 3x BTC perp because perp shorts pay 0% financing in this engine while equity shorts carry a ~7% all-in drag.
novelty: The edge hypothesis is that persistent risk premia paid as income - credit spreads, repo/MBS spread, FX interest differentials, option and VIX-futures roll premium, and the cash rate itself - accrue with time rather than with direction, so the book's return driver is the passage of days rather than a rerating of growth expectations. That is structurally different from long-AI-momentum: there is not a single technology name in the book, gross equity beta is roughly 0.25, and the largest legs are floating-rate instruments whose payoff is indifferent to whether the AI trade extends or breaks. It is falsified if the book's P&L turns out to be explained by beta to SPY or by the direction of BTC rather than by accrual - concretely, if in a flat-to-down equity tape the income legs fail to grind out a positive return, or if a credit/vol shock produces a drawdown larger than the annual carry being collected, which is the standing risk of every short-tail carry strategy.

positions.thesis: AAA CLO tranches: a floating-rate spread of roughly 130bp over SOFR with near-zero duration. The anchor leg - the highest-quality way to earn above the engine's 4% cash and the reason the book's drawdowns stay small.

BBB/BB CLO mezzanine at roughly 9% floating yield. Same loan collateral as JAAA, but paid for taking subordination instead of duration - a deliberate second helping of the same carry at a higher point on the risk curve.

Agency mortgage REIT - the listed form of the pure carry trade: borrow at repo, hold government-guaranteed MBS, earn the spread at roughly 6x leverage. Credit risk is federal; the risk being paid for is funding and convexity.
Equity variance risk premium: writes S&P index calls and distributes the premium, converting index upside into roughly 12% realized income. Owns the premium, not the momentum.
Midstream MLPs at roughly 7.5% distribution yield off fee-based, volume-linked pipeline cash flows - a real-asset cash yield whose driver is throughput contracts rather than credit spreads.

EM local-currency sovereign debt - the textbook FX carry trade, long high-policy-rate EM currencies against USD funding, at roughly 6.5% yield. The one leg whose carry is an interest differential rather than a credit spread.
EM USD sovereign spread. Deliberately splits EM carry into its two independent halves - currency risk in EMLC, hard-currency default spread here - so one can survive the other.
US high-yield corporate spread at roughly 7% yield and short duration - the plain-vanilla corporate credit risk premium, held small because it is the most crowded of the spread carries.

VIX-futures roll yield: -0.5x front VIX futures harvests the persistent contango between spot VIX and the first two futures. The half-leverage structure caps the tail that destroys 1x short-vol vehicles, and a 25% stop caps it again - in the 2025H1 backtest that stop did fire and converted a -35% leg into a 1.6% NAV cost.

A financing-spread expression, not a price view. Reading the engine, perp shorts are charged 0% funding while perp longs pay 10% APR on notional and equity shorts pay 3% borrow on top of 4% forgone cash yield - so short beta is roughly seven points a year cheaper in perp form. 9% of notional hedge for 3% of NAV in margin, with liquidation and the 65% stop capping the loss at that margin.

backtest.notes: Run through tracker/round2.py --backtest on the exact file registered here; numbers are verbatim. The book trailed SPY in all three windows but took roughly 40% of SPY's drawdown (-3.65 vs -8.88 in 2026H1, -1.50 vs -5.07 in 2025H2), which is the expected shape of carry. Honest attribution: the largest single contributor in both mandated windows was the BTC perp short (+2.62% of NAV in 2026H1, +2.29% in 2025H2), and that is directional luck, not carry - BTC fell 29% and 26% in those windows, and the engine pays a short perp nothing for holding it. In 2025H1, when BTC rose, the same leg cost -0.70%. Strip the perp and the book returns roughly 4.3% and 7.0% in the two mandated windows. The genuine carry engine was NLY (+2.12% of NAV in 2025H2), SVXY (+1.62% in 2025H2, but stopped out for -1.6% in 2025H1), AMLP (+1.85% in 2026H1) and the steady 2.4-3.1%-per-half grind from JAAA and CLOZ. Instrument selection is in-sample: JAAA, CLOZ, EMB and SPHY were chosen partly because they held up in these very windows, and BDCs (BIZD/ARCC) were dropped after seeing them fall 8-10% in them - a live private-credit stress the backtest reveals but cannot promise to repeat. Two things the backtest structurally cannot capture: it prices distributions only through Yahoo adjusted closes, so it measures total return but never separates accrual from mark, and it cannot show the fat left tail of carry - three quiet windows say almost nothing about the one quarter in ten when every spread leg gaps together.

outlook: I expect a slow, low-variance grind of roughly 0.5-0.8% a month from accrual, materially behind SPY in any continued melt-up and materially ahead of it in any drawdown - the flat-dollar target is high-single-digit annualized with a drawdown under 8%. Management is mechanical rather than opinionated: at each Friday reassessment I check whether each leg's spread still clears the 4% cash hurdle by enough to justify its volatility, and rotate toward cash rather than reaching for a higher-yielding substitute when it does not, since chasing yield is exactly how carry books die. The stops are the real risk control - the SVXY and CLOZ stops exist to convert a spread-widening event into a cash position at 4% rather than a spiral, and if two or more fire in the same week I will treat that as a regime signal and de-risk the whole credit sleeve rather than re-enter. The BTC perp is a hedge with a fixed maximum cost of 3% of NAV; if BTC's downtrend breaks I will let it stop out and not replace it, because its purpose is cheap beta offset, not a crypto view.
